unit.title: School Life & Schedules: Ordinals, Subjects, and Time

lesson.title: Reading Two Real-Style School Schedules from Latin America
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you named subjects and put them in order. Today you read the real thing: two class schedules — dos horarios — like the ones students carry in Mexico and Colombia. You do not need to understand every word. You need to find information: which materia meets when, how long the descanso is, what time the day starts.

A schedule is a table, so read it like one. Scan the time column down the left, then read across to the subject. Words that help you navigate:

- el horario — the schedule
- la hora — the time / the class hour
- de lunes a viernes — Monday to Friday
- el descanso / el recreo — the break

And notice the clock. In much of Latin America the school day starts early — often between 6:30 and 7:15 in the morning — and a shorter day can end around 1:00 in the afternoon.

HORARIO A — Escuela Secundaria "Benito Juárez", México. Primer semestre, de lunes a viernes.

- 7:00 – 7:50 — Español
- 7:50 – 8:40 — Matemáticas
- 8:40 – 9:30 — Ciencias Naturales
- 9:30 – 9:50 — Descanso
- 9:50 – 10:40 — Inglés
- 10:40 – 11:30 — Geografía
- 11:30 – 12:20 — Educación Física
- 12:20 – 1:10 — Artes

The first class is Español at 7:00. The descanso is 20 minutes, right after the third class.

HORARIO B — Colegio San Martín, Colombia. Grado sexto, de lunes a viernes.

- 6:30 – 7:20 — Matemáticas
- 7:20 – 8:10 — Lengua Castellana
- 8:10 – 9:00 — Ciencias Naturales
- 9:00 – 9:30 — Descanso
- 9:30 – 10:20 — Ciencias Sociales
- 10:20 – 11:10 — Inglés
- 11:10 – 12:00 — Educación Física
- 12:00 – 12:50 — Educación Artística

Two names to decode: Lengua Castellana is the Spanish class (language and reading), and Ciencias Sociales combines history and geography in one subject. This day starts at 6:30 — earlier than Horario A — and the descanso is 30 minutes.

Read for answers, in Spanish where you can:

- ¿A qué hora empieza el Horario B? (6:30)
- ¿Cuál es la segunda materia en el Horario A? (Matemáticas)
- En el Horario A, ¿qué clase tienes justo después del descanso? (Inglés)
- ¿Qué descanso es más largo, el del Horario A o el del Horario B? (el del Horario B, 30 minutos)
- En el Horario B, 'Lengua Castellana' es la clase de... (español)

The activity and worksheet have more. The skill today is finding facts in an authentic text, not translating it.

You pulled real information out of two schedules written for native speakers — start times, subject order, break length. Tomorrow you move from facts to opinions: which materia is interesante, which one is aburrida, and why.

questions.q: According to Horario A, what is the first class of the day?
questions.explanation: Horario A starts with Español at 7:00. Matemáticas is the second class, from 7:50 to 8:40.

questions.q: En el Horario B, ¿a qué hora empieza la primera clase?
questions.explanation: Horario B (Colombia) begins at 6:30 with Matemáticas — earlier than Horario A.

questions.q: In Horario A, which class comes right after the descanso?
questions.explanation: The descanso is 9:30–9:50, and Inglés follows from 9:50 to 10:40.

options: el Horario B no tiene descanso
questions.explanation: Horario A's break is 9:30–9:50 (20 minutes); Horario B's is 9:00–9:30 (30 minutes).

questions.q: In Horario B, 'Lengua Castellana' is the class for which subject?
questions.explanation: In Colombia the Spanish class is often called Lengua Castellana. 'Ciencias Sociales' is the one that combines history and geography.

objectives: Locate specific information in an authentic-style Spanish class schedule: start time, the order of subjects, and the length and placement of the descanso
Interpret culture-specific subject names (Lengua Castellana = Spanish class; Ciencias Sociales = history and geography) from context
Notice real differences between a Latin American school day and their own, especially the early start time
materialsNeeded: Printed or projected copies of Horario A and Horario B
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review the ordinals and school words from Day 1 with one quick oral round.
2. Teach the navigation words (el horario, la hora, de lunes a viernes, el descanso) and the 'read it like a table' strategy.
3. Read Horario A together. Ask the built-in questions; students point to the row that answers each one.
4. Read Horario B. Decode Lengua Castellana and Ciencias Sociales from context before giving the answer. Compare the two start times.
5. Discuss: what surprised you about these schedules? (start time, single long break, subjects combined)
6. Complete the multiple-choice activity.
7. Complete the worksheet.
8. Preview tomorrow's opinion exchange.
differentiationTips: Struggling: give them only Horario A and three questions; highlight the time column first so the table structure is visible
Ready for more: have them write three new Spanish comprehension questions about Horario B for a partner to answer
If a student stalls trying to translate every subject name, redirect: 'You do not need every word — which row has the time the question asks about?'
teacherGuide.answerKey: Horario A: first class Español (7:00); second class Matemáticas; class after the descanso is Inglés; break is 20 minutes. Horario B: starts 6:30; Lengua Castellana = the Spanish class; Ciencias Sociales = history + geography; break is 30 minutes (longer than A's). Multiple choice: 1. Español, 2. a las 6:30, 3. Inglés, 4. Horario B (30 minutos), 5. Spanish (language and reading).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: This is the core WA-WL-2015.1.2 Interpretive Reading task for the week: students extract meaning from an authentic-format document written for native speakers, using layout and cognates rather than full translation, exactly as the scope-and-sequence Day 2 design specifies ('read two authentic-style school schedules from Latin America; answer comprehension questions'). The culture-specific subject names and early start also seed weeks 11 and 34's comparison work.

worksheet.title: Reading Two Real-Style School Schedules from Latin America

generationData.instructions: Use Horario A (México) and Horario B (Colombia) to answer. You do not need to translate every word — find the row that answers the question.

rows.problem: What time does each schedule start, and which one starts earlier: Horario A or Horario B?
List the subjects in Horario A in order, first to last.
How long is the descanso in each schedule? Which is longer?
In Horario B, what everyday subjects do 'Lengua Castellana' and 'Ciencias Sociales' stand for?
Name one way a Latin American school day in these schedules is different from yours.
